themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints surged to 13 THIS WEEK, a 373% increase from the 8-week baseline average of 2.8 per week (z-score: 8.55), signaling a potential uptick in quality-of-life disturbances or enforcement gaps that warrant immediate investigation.
evidence: 13 Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (373% increase)
Z-score of 8.55 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No context provided on nature of complaints—suggests diverse underlying issues
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD 70th Precinct on whether they've seen uptick in specific offense categories or quality-of-life issues
Canvass residents in hotspot blocks to identify common complaints: noise disturbances, street harassment, loitering, or other triggers

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal & Sanitation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential Disposal Complaints jumped to 22 THIS WEEK, a 309% spike from the 5.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.47), coinciding with a 593% surge in Street Sweeping Complaints last week (13 vs. 1.9 avg), suggesting a potential collection or street cleanliness breakdown.
evidence: 22 Residential Disposal Complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average (309% increase, z-score: 5.47)
13 Street Sweeping Complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (593% increase, z-score: 6.07)
Convergence of two sanitation-adjacent complaint categories suggests systemic collection or cleaning failure
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation for explanations of missed pickups or street sweeping delays in recent week
Map complaint locations to identify whether specific neighborhoods or routes are affected disproportionately
Interview residents on curbside pileup, pest activity, and impact on block conditions

themes_detail.label: Street Noise & Enforcement Vacuum
themes_detail.summary: Street/Sidewalk Noise Complaints exploded to 54 last week, a 300% jump from the 13.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.62), while Real Time Enforcement complaints doubled to 9 THIS WEEK (260% above baseline), suggesting residents perceive insufficient police or DOE response to disturbances.
evidence: 54 Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints last week vs. 13.5 weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 7.62)
9 Real Time Enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average (260% increase, z-score: 5.31)
Temporal cluster suggests noise problem + perceived enforcement failure in same 2-week window
reporting_angles: Identify what types of noise dominate complaints: construction, vehicles, street vendors, social gatherings, or music venues
Interview residents on frequency of noise, times of day, and whether 311 or police calls resulted in visible action
Check NYPD citation data for noise violations and response times in past week

themes_detail.label: Illegal Pet Complaints Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Animal Kept as Pet complaints skyrocketed to 3 approximately 2 weeks ago, a stunning 2300% increase from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69), possibly indicating a new pet ownership trend, illegal breeding operation, or community concern about zoning violations.
evidence: 3 Illegal Animal Kept as Pet complaints ~2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Extreme z-score indicates this is a genuine anomaly, not seasonal fluctuation
Small absolute number limits data richness but signal is statistically robust
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints target specific animals (roosters, exotic species, livestock) or a single property/operation
Check with NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene for any new animal welfare complaints or inspections in Midwood/Ocean Parkway
Interview residents and civic leaders on whether there's a known illegal breeding or farm operation in the district

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Infrastructure Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Traffic Signal Condition complaints spiked to 129 two weeks ago, a 303% increase from the 32.0 weekly average (z-score: 6.42), indicating potential widespread signal failures that may affect pedestrian safety and traffic flow across the district.
evidence: 129 Traffic Signal Condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 32.0 weekly average (303% increase, z-score: 6.42)
High-visibility infrastructure complaint with direct public safety implications
Timing suggests potential weather event, power disruption, or system-wide maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify whether signal failures are clustered on specific avenues (e.g., Ocean Parkway, Flatbush Ave, Nostrand)
Contact NYC DOT about signal outages, repair timelines, and whether a weather event or infrastructure incident triggered the spike
Interview pedestrians and cyclists on near-misses or unsafe intersections due to malfunctioning signals
